description: The last step of the lifecycle, and the only one the requestor takes after approval. Submitting the satisfaction form marks the request COMPLETED. The old app shipped this as a single acknowledgement button; this spec keeps that as the contract and adds the rating and comment the form is named after.

happy_path.action: sees the CSM banner on an approved request
rates the service and optionally comments

happy_path.result: csm.submittedAt is set, completionStatus and masterStatus both become COMPLETED, in one transaction
the status chip reads Completed, the banner is gone, and the signed PDF is available

alternate_paths.name: Already submitted
alternate_paths.result: a completed state showing when the feedback was submitted, with no form and no way to submit twice

alternate_paths.name: No CSM record
alternate_paths.trigger: the request was never finally approved
alternate_paths.result: the page redirects back to the request detail rather than rendering an empty form

alternate_paths.name: Not the owner
alternate_paths.trigger: anyone but the requestor opens the URL
alternate_paths.result: getMyCsm returns null and the page redirects; submitCsm refuses with NOT_FOUND

alternate_paths.name: SUBMIT_CSM revoked
alternate_paths.result: the submit control is disabled with a reason and the procedure refuses

alternate_paths.name: Double submit
alternate_paths.result: the second call finds submittedAt already set and returns CONFLICT; the request stays COMPLETED once

models.name: Csm
models.prisma_note: Adds the two fields that make it a satisfaction form rather than an acknowledgement. Both are nullable so the rows created by spec 014 remain valid

trpc_procedures.name: getMyCsm
guards: returns null unless the caller owns the request
returns null when no Csm row exists
trpc_procedures.description: Null rather than an error, because the page's correct response to both cases is the same redirect. Ownership is checked against the session.

trpc_procedures.name: submitCsm
guards: the Csm row must not already have submittedAt
trpc_procedures.description: Writes rating, comment and submittedAt on the Csm row and sets completionStatus and masterStatus to COMPLETED on the request, in one transaction.

forms.name: CsmForm
forms.success_message: Thank you. Your request is now complete.
forms.error_message: Failed to submit your feedback. Please try again.

fields.name: rating
fields.label: How satisfied are you with how this request was handled?
fields.note: AppRating, 1-5. Required — a satisfaction form with an optional satisfaction measure collects nothing.

fields.name: comment
fields.label: Anything you would like to add?

functional: The CSM record is created by the final director approval (spec 014), never by this page. A request that was never finally approved has no CSM and the page redirects.
Submitting sets submittedAt, rating and comment on the Csm row and completionStatus and masterStatus to COMPLETED on the request, in one transaction.
COMPLETED is the terminal happy state. Nothing follows it.
The rating is required and the comment is optional.
Feedback can be submitted exactly once. The completed state replaces the form afterwards and shows what was given.
The signed PDF stays available after completion — completing the request does not close it.
Adding rating and comment as nullable columns keeps the rows created before this spec valid; a CSM submitted under the old contract simply has no rating.
authorization: Route gate: assertAuthenticatedFn. The real gate is ownership, which the route cannot express.
Server gate on getMyCsm: returns null for anyone but the owner, so the page redirects rather than confirming the request exists.
Server gate on submitCsm: ownership, then assertPermission(SUBMIT_CSM), then completionStatus must be CSM_PENDING, then submittedAt must be null.
No staff role may submit a requestor's feedback — that would make the measure worthless. Staff are refused by the ownership check, not by a role gate.
The banner being hidden for a non-owner is not a gate; both procedures check independently.
ux: The page says what submitting does before it is pressed: this completes the request.
The rating control is the first thing on the page and is large enough to press on a phone.
The completed state thanks the requestor and shows the date and what they gave, rather than a bare 'already submitted'.
The submit button shows a pending state and is disabled during the call, so a double press cannot produce a CONFLICT the user has to interpret.
A redirect away from the page (no CSM record) is silent — landing back on the request is the correct answer and an error toast would only confuse.

server_guards.guard: the request exists and request.userId === ctx.user.id

server_guards.error: FORBIDDEN — You don't have permission to perform this action
FORBIDDEN — The feedback form is not available for this request

server_guards.guard: the Csm row's submittedAt is null
server_guards.error: CONFLICT — Feedback has already been submitted

covers: the owner of a CSM_PENDING request can submit and the request becomes COMPLETED
submitting writes rating, comment and submittedAt in the same transaction as the request update
a second submit returns CONFLICT and leaves submittedAt unchanged
submitting for a request that is not CSM_PENDING is FORBIDDEN
a DIRECTOR submitting gets NOT_FOUND — ownership, not role
a user without SUBMIT_CSM gets FORBIDDEN
getMyCsm returns null for a non-owner
getMyCsm returns null when no Csm row exists
the CSM banner on an approved request leads to the form
submitting marks the request Completed and removes the banner
revisiting the page shows the completed state with the rating given
opening the CSM URL for a request that was never approved redirects to the request

acceptance_criteria.given: an APPROVED request with completionStatus CSM_PENDING
acceptance_criteria.when: the owner submits a rating of 4
acceptance_criteria.then: the Csm row has submittedAt and rating 4, and the request's masterStatus and completionStatus are both COMPLETED
the completed state is shown with the date and the rating, and no form

acceptance_criteria.given: a request that was never finally approved
acceptance_criteria.then: they are redirected to the request detail page

acceptance_criteria.when: they call csm.submitCsm for someone's request

acceptance_criteria.then: the first succeeds and the second returns CONFLICT; the request is COMPLETED exactly once
the fully signed document still renders

edge_cases: The Csm row exists before the form is ever opened, created by the approval. This page updates it; it must never create one, or a request could gain a CSM without being approved.
rating and comment must be nullable, or the migration breaks every Csm row created by spec 014 before this spec ships.
getMyCsm returning null for both 'not yours' and 'does not exist' is deliberate — it keeps the endpoint from confirming whether a request id exists.
COMPLETED must be written to masterStatus as well as completionStatus, or the requestor's list still shows Approved after they have finished.
The submit is the second half of a two-part contract with spec 014; if the CSM_PENDING check is ever loosened, an unapproved request can be marked complete.
AppRating must be controlled by RHF through its binding, not by local state, or the required-rating validation never sees a value.
out_of_scope: Reporting or aggregation of satisfaction scores — nothing reads the ratings yet, and the office has not asked for a report.
Reminders to complete the CSM — there is no notification system.
Editing feedback after submission — it is submitted once, deliberately.
A CSM for a rejected request — feedback is only requested when a request was approved.
